Displacement = √(600² + 800²) = 1000 m. Total time = 200 s. Magnitude of average velocity = 1000 / 200 = 5.0 m s⁻¹.

content.text: A stone is thrown from the top of a vertical cliff with a speed of 12 m s⁻¹ at an angle of 30°
the horizontal. The stone is released 15 m above the sea. Air resistance is negligible.
What is the horizontal distance from the base of the cliff to the point where the stone hits the sea?
Uses the whole velocity instead of the horizontal component: 12 × 1.24 = 14.9 m
Ignores the initial vertical velocity (solves it like a horizontal projection): t = 1.75 s, 10.4 × 1.75 = 18.2 m
Solves as if the stone were thrown upwards at an angle: t = 2.47 s, 10.4 × 2.47 = 25.6 m

Downward positive. Initial vertical velocity = 12 sin 30° = 6.0 m s⁻¹; horizontal velocity = 12 cos 30° = 10.4 m s⁻¹. 15 = 6.0t + 4.9t² → t = 1.24 s. Horizontal distance = 10.4 × 1.24 = 12.9 m ≈ 13 m.
